backup_target: ZERO by default; one optional private fallback only when primary fails source rights or clarity
gates: Subject: exact canonical physical object only. If a paten is requested, a chalice may not appear in the published hero photo.
No unrelated liturgical vessels, tools, hands, museum labels or surrounding display objects competing with the subject. Minor display supports are separately noted, not automatically approved.
Plain neutral/dark background strongly preferred. Visible edges, complete silhouette, natural light, sharpness and true material colour.
Catholic traditional Roman-rite identification checked; do not substitute Byzantine or Protestant, generic unlabeled linens or viaticum accessories.
Full image must portray the object itself, not an action or grouping unless canonical ID explicitly defines a matched set or scene.
Original file rights, photographer, exact Commons source and licence tracked. Photographic crop/derivative must retain original provenance and respect licence; never invent visual evidence.
One provisional assistant choice does not confer user aesthetic approval, liturgical certification or publication rights approval.
If no source satisfies the gate, leave the hero empty and retain a precise acquisition instruction rather than publishing the best bad option.
exceptions: AL07 intentionally six matching candlesticks as one canonical set
AL16 three altar cards as one canonical set
AL17/AL18 are directional annotations on an authenticated altar image, not separate objects

selections.label: High altar
selections.background: Historic church sanctuary wall murals, reredos and statuary integral to architectural high-altar setting; no additional freestanding forward altar table.
selections.selection_rationale: One complete traditional fixed high altar photographed head-on in St Martin Catholic church, Castelnau-d'Estrétefonds, France (1848). The altar is coherent and intact, its tabernacle centred, six matching gilded candles three per side, altar stone and frontal visible; B26 7360x4912 original pixels assessed. A real altar cannot be detached from its church like a museum vessel. One scene as architecture, not a composite of unrelated objects.
selections.qa_outstanding: Architectural exception is explicitly assistant-provisional: image contains integrated tabernacle, crucifix and candles. No separate hero credits for these other object IDs. User editorial approval for background context and photo aesthetics is still required. CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution and licence-adaptations rules apply.

selections.qa_outstanding: Image of a current church tabernacle rather than typical ancient high-altar tabernacle. Confirm editorial preference for its simpler modern cylindrical style. CC BY 4.0 credit and crop modification notice required. Publication remains unapproved.

selections.label: Wine cruet
selections.background: Sacristy linen and soft-focus liturgical furnishing only; other matching water cruet cropped from source.
selections.selection_rationale: Source original photograph of clear-glass paired Catholic Mass cruets. Wine vessel occupies right side and is distinguishable from water vessel by amber/golden wine. Authentic ordinary glass Mass cruet shape is more instructive for the 1962 TLM than an uncommon medieval metal example. Derived crop transparently isolates wine cruet from the original pair; no photomontage or invented object.
selections.qa_outstanding: Derived crop only 683×1196; soft-focus sacred furnishings remain in background. Though physical type suits 1962 Mass, source image does not independently document a particular TLM celebration. User visual and liturgical acceptance pending.

explicitly_disqualified_hero_sources.why: Two cruets in same image; individual wine cruet unidentified.

b20.selection_rule: One exact object, visually recognizable, no unrelated articles in frame, clean background.

architectural_exception_policy: High altar, church steps, Communion rail, gradine and retable are not portable objects; allow one complete in-situ architectural subject without deceptive scene recomposition. Retain the strict single-object standard for vessels, bells, books, free-standing furniture and vestments. Assistant-provisional selection is not user editorial or publication approval.
photo_role_policy: One actual Commons source photograph can yield truthful single-object derived crops for two matching physical objects. Derived crops do not count as two independent source photographs and must retain common original source URI, sha256, and clearly disclosed crop coordinates. Only assistant-provisional, not user-approved or published.
